questions.q: Which API-name suffix identifies a Platform Event object, as opposed to a custom object?
options: __mdt
questions.explain: Platform Event API names always end in __e, parallel to __c for custom objects/fields and __mdt for custom metadata types.

questions.q: Can you run a SOQL SELECT to retrieve the past activity of a platform event after it has been delivered?
options: Yes, platform events are stored exactly like custom object rows
No, platform events are published and delivered, not stored as queryable, updatable rows
Only if the platform event is standard-volume
Only from an external system, never from Apex
questions.explain: Platform events are not queryable rows the way Account or a custom object is. Once delivered (and outside the retention window covered in Lesson 6), the event is gone.

questions.q: Since API version 45.0, what is the default volume type for a newly defined custom platform event?
options: Standard-volume
High-volume
There is no default; you must always choose explicitly
It depends on the org's edition
questions.explain: High-volume is the default for new custom event definitions starting in API version 45.0, and standard-volume custom events are being phased out.

questions.q: An 'Order Confirmed' platform event will be acted on by an external fulfillment system that must trust the order data is durable. Which Publish Behavior setting fits this event?
options: Publish Immediately, so the event fires as fast as possible
Publish After Commit, so the event only fires once the transaction has actually committed
Publish Behavior has no effect on whether subscriber data is trustworthy
Neither option matters for high-volume events
questions.explain: Publish After Commit only publishes once the enclosing transaction commits successfully, which is the right choice whenever a subscriber needs to trust the underlying data is durable.

questions.q: Which of these field types is NOT something you can add directly to a platform event the way you would on a custom object?
options: A Text field
A Number field
A Date field
A Lookup relationship field
questions.explain: Platform events don't support relationship fields like lookups or master-detail — they carry simple data fields (text, number, date, checkbox, picklist, etc.), not record relationships.
